lessons.title: Metro vs Non-Metro: The 50% and 40% Rule and Which Cities Qualify

body.text: Living in a 50% city does not automatically mean a bigger exemption. The city percentage only matters when Limit 3 is the one holding you back, and for most people paying moderate rent, it is not.

children.text: When the draft Income-tax Rules, 2026 proposed adding Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad to the 50% list, many salaried employees in all four cities read it as a straightforward tax cut. For some of them it was worth tens of thousands of rupees a year. For many others it changed nothing at all. This lesson shows you which group you are in.

markDefs.definition: The rule under the Income-tax Rules, 1962 that set the HRA limits for Section 10(13A). It named only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai for the 50% limit and still applies to income up to 31 March 2026.

children.text: Limit 3 is 50% of salary if your rented home is in one of the cities named in Rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, and 40% of salary everywhere else. Rule 279 replaced
of the 1962 Rules, which named only four cities.

cells: Every other city, town and village

body.title: Quick Check: On the List?
body.question: For rent paid in tax year 2026-27, which of these locations qualifies for the 50% limit?
body.explanation: Ahmedabad is one of the four cities added by Rule 279. Gurugram, Navi Mumbai and Noida are separate cities with their own municipal bodies and are not named in the rule, however close they are to Delhi or Mumbai. They stay at 40%.

children.text: The 50% or 40% figure only enters your exemption through Limit 3. If Limit 1 (your HRA) or Limit 2 (rent minus 10% of salary) is already below 40% of salary, the city makes no difference. Working through the three limits gives a simple test.

body.label: The 50% list raises your exemption only if both are true
body.value: HRA > 40% of salary AND rent > 50% of salary
body.context: If either condition fails, a 50% city and a 40% city give you exactly the same exemption. The most the 50% list can ever add is 10% of salary.

body.caption: H = HRA received, R = rent paid, S = salary for HRA

body.title: Harish in Pune: salary ₹12,00,000, HRA ₹6,00,000, rent ₹7,20,000 a year

children.text: Harish's HRA is 50% of salary and his rent is 60% of salary, so he passes both tests. His exemption rises by ₹1,20,000, the maximum possible 10% of salary. In the 30% slab, that saves him about ₹37,440 a year. His colleague Priya, on the same pay but renting a ₹25,000 flat in Gachibowli, Hyderabad, fails the rent test: her Limit 2 is ₹1,80,000, well below 40% of salary. Her exemption is ₹1,80,000 whether Hyderabad is on the list or not.

body.title: Extra annual exemption from the 50% list, on Harish's pay

children.text: On a salary of ₹1 lakh a month, the city makes no difference until rent crosses ₹50,000 a month. The gain then grows until it hits the ₹1,20,000 cap at ₹60,000 of rent, and stays flat beyond that.
City Limits: Where the Rule Goes Quiet

Rule 279 simply names the eight cities. It does not define their boundaries. That is clear enough for most addresses, but India's large cities spill into neighbouring municipal areas, and the rule does not say how far each city reaches.

Separate municipal corporations, not named in the rule
A separate city across the Hooghly, not named in the rule
Areas under a neighbouring municipal body, such as Pimpri-Chinchwad near Pune
Pune and other newly added cities
Some treat them as part of the wider city, others do not. The rule gives no guidance

body.text: If your rented home is on the edge of one of the eight cities, check which municipal body your address falls under, and ask how your employer is treating it. If the answer is not clear, the cautious approach is to use 40%. Claiming 50% for an address that is later found to be outside city limits can lead to the extra exemption being withdrawn, with tax and interest.

body.title: Scenario: Mulund or Thane?
body.scenario: Meghna works at an office in Thane and is choosing between two similar 2BHKs: one in Mulund, inside Mumbai city limits, at ₹48,000 a month, and one in Thane at ₹42,000 a month. Her basic salary is ₹1,00,000 a month, her HRA is ₹50,000 a month, and she is in the 30% slab under the old regime. A colleague says "take Mulund, Mumbai is a 50% city, the tax saving covers the extra rent."
body.prompt: Work out her exempt HRA in each flat. How much of the difference is due to the city, and what does Mulund really cost her?
body.modelAnswer: Salary ₹12,00,000, HRA ₹6,00,000. Mulund (50%): Limit 2 is ₹5,76,000 minus ₹1,20,000 = ₹4,56,000; Limit 3 is ₹6,00,000; exempt HRA ₹4,56,000. Thane (40%): Limit 2 is ₹5,04,000 minus ₹1,20,000 = ₹3,84,000; Limit 3 is ₹4,80,000; exempt HRA ₹3,84,000. The exemption is ₹72,000 higher in Mulund, but none of that comes from the city. In both flats Limit 2 binds, and Thane would give her exactly ₹3,84,000 even if it were a 50% city. The whole difference comes from paying ₹72,000 more rent. The extra exemption saves about ₹22,464 in tax, so Mulund costs her ₹49,536 more a year in net terms. Pick the flat for location and comfort, not for the city label.

body.title: Try It: What Ahmedabad Joining the List Is Worth
body.prompt: Sanjay rents a flat in Satellite, Ahmedabad for ₹50,000 a month. His basic salary is ₹80,000 a month and his HRA is ₹40,000 a month, with no DA or commission. By how much does his annual exempt HRA increase in tax year 2026-27, compared with the same figures under the old 40% rule? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: Salary ₹9,60,000, HRA ₹4,80,000, rent ₹6,00,000. Limit 2 is ₹6,00,000 minus ₹96,000 = ₹5,04,000. At 40%, Limit 3 is ₹3,84,000, which is the smallest, so the exemption is ₹3,84,000. At 50%, Limit 3 is ₹4,80,000, now equal to Limit 1, so the exemption is ₹4,80,000. The increase is ₹96,000, the full 10% of his salary, because his HRA is 50% of salary and his rent is well above 50% of salary.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Rent Test
body.textWithBlank: A 50% city can only increase your HRA exemption if your annual rent is more than ___% of your salary for HRA.
body.explanation: For Limit 3 at 40% to be the smallest, rent minus 10% of salary must exceed 40% of salary, which means rent must exceed 50% of salary. Your HRA must also exceed 40% of salary.

body.text: Employers often set HRA at 40% of basic outside the four old metros. If your HRA is still 40% of basic after moving into a newly added city, the 50% list cannot help you, because Limit 1 caps the exemption at 40% of salary anyway. Ask HR whether the pay structure will be updated for Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad.

body.title: Does the 50% List Help You?
steps: Look up the address on your rent agreement and confirm the city and municipal body it falls under
Check whether that city is one of the eight named in Rule 279
Calculate your HRA as a percentage of your salary for HRA. Is it more than 40%?
Calculate your annual rent as a percentage of your salary for HRA. Is it more than 50%?
If both answers are yes and you are in a listed city, work out your gain: the smaller of HRA, rent minus 10% of salary and 50% of salary, minus 40% of salary
If your address is on a city boundary, confirm with your employer how it is being treated and keep a copy of any written reply

cards.definition: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad, named in Rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, from tax year 2026-27.
The 1962 rule that set HRA limits under the old Act. Its 50% list had only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai, and it still governs income up to March 2026.
A 50% city raises the exemption only if HRA is more than 40% of salary and rent is more than 50% of salary.
The 50% list can add at most 10% of salary for HRA to the annual exemption.
Places like Gurugram, Noida, Thane and Navi Mumbai that are separate cities next to a metro. They are not named in Rule 279 and use 40%.

points: From tax year 2026-27, Limit 3 is 50% of salary in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad, and 40% everywhere else
Income up to 31 March 2026 still follows the old four-city list under Rule 2A
The city only matters when Limit 3 binds, which needs HRA above 40% of salary and rent above 50% of salary
The 50% list can add at most 10% of salary to your annual exemption
Satellite cities such as Gurugram, Noida, Thane and Navi Mumbai are not on the list. Boundary areas of the eight cities are unsettled, so be cautious
If your employer still pays HRA at 40% of basic in a newly added city, the 50% list cannot raise your exemption

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or financial advice. It reflects Rule 279 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 as understood at the time of writing. The rule does not define city boundaries, and treatment of border areas may be clarified later. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
